If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in mid-period (8–14 days), increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for mid-horizon to capture momentum.

If sentiment is low (≤0.33) in late period (15–30 days), apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias to prevent late-stage overcorrection.

If sentiment transitions from low to high over 3–5 days, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% in the 7–14 day window to reflect sentiment shift.

If sentiment is uniformly low across 18+ days, apply a 1.0–2.0% downward correction to all forecast points, especially late horizon (15–30 days).

If sentiment shows strong upward trend (≥0.67 for 3+ consecutive days), increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to reflect bullish sentiment.
